title: CPU is Running How FAST??? #techtok #learnontiktok #tiktoklearningcam...
summary: Windows switched its timing source from the modern CPU Time Stamp Counter (TSC) to the legacy chipset High Precision Event Timer (HPET via useplatformclock), causing inaccurate timing and severe CPU scheduling bottlenecks.
symptoms: Opened Task Manager Performance tab: observed 70% CPU utilization with only 5% GPU utilization.
Swapped the RTX 5070 with a GTX 1660 Super; observed identical low frame rates (~150 FPS), confirming a CPU-side bottleneck.
Checked CPU clock speed readout in Task Manager and found erroneous readings exceeding 1 billion to 15 billion GHz.
Identified the symptom as a corrupted Windows timer configuration using HPET (High Precision Event Timer) instead of the CPU's TSC (Time Stamp Counter).

fix_steps.title: Opened Task Manager Performance tab
fix_steps.detail: observed 70% CPU utilization with only 5% GPU utilization.

fix_steps.title: Diagnostic Action 2
fix_steps.detail: Swapped the RTX 5070 with a GTX 1660 Super; observed identical low frame rates (~150 FPS), confirming a CPU-side bottleneck.

fix_steps.detail: Checked CPU clock speed readout in Task Manager and found erroneous readings exceeding 1 billion to 15 billion GHz.

fix_steps.title: Diagnostic Action 4
fix_steps.detail: Identified the symptom as a corrupted Windows timer configuration using HPET (High Precision Event Timer) instead of the CPU's TSC (Time Stamp Counter).

fix_steps.title: Final Resolution
